bullets.title: Hot CPI Print Forces Fed Repricing; Dec/Mar Hikes Now Base Case
bullets.body: October core CPI came in at +0.30% m/m (consensus 0.22%) and headline at +0.35%, the third consecutive hot print, pushing core PCE tracking to ~0.35% m/m and 3.3% y/y. Markets re-priced sharply, with 28-43bps of hikes now expected for Dec/Jan vs. 1 hike priced the prior day; 22V sees 25bp hikes in Dec and March as baseline with January increasingly live. Fed Governor Waller flagged 50bp risk, though most analysts view that as unlikely given Fed's aversion to directional policy shifts.

bullets.title: Market Positioning Washed Out — Mechanical Setup for Squeeze
bullets.body: Goldman prime brokerage data shows L/S gross leverage at the 26th percentile and nets at the 1st percentile entering the week, suggesting deleveraging is largely complete. CTAs flipped net short and $2.2B flowed into SOXL (2nd-largest daily inflow on record) Thursday; Jefferies notes S&P spot down + VIX down historically precedes +4.2% one-month returns. Despite the rates headwind, the technical setup argues for a potential mechanical squeeze if vol normalizes.

bullets.title: S&P +1.2%, SOXX +5.2% Pre-Market; AI Infra Complex Broadly Rallies
bullets.body: Pre-market S&P futures +0.98% to ~7,611, with semiconductors and AI infrastructure leading: MRVL +8.5%, INTC +5.9%, AMD +5.7%, WDC +8.1%, STX +8.9%. The rally is driven by CRWV's strong earnings, OpenAI revenue beat, and improving AI capex confidence after post-midterm selling exhaustion. VIX jumped 8.8% to 17.74 on the session, reflecting ongoing vol risk even as equities bid.

bullets.title: CRWV Earnings Allay AI Overbuild Fears; $9B Prepayments Underpin Financing
bullets.body: CoreWeave raised FY guidance, confirmed capacity sold out through 2027, and outlined $9B in customer pre-payments and deposits expected over the next three months, addressing the core bear case on funding. Parent-level capital raise stays below $5B through 2027, with >75% of 2027 capex fundable from backlog; the company pivots to asset-backed/DDTL secured debt and won't access unsecured markets. CRWV +13-15% pre-market; PT raised to $149 at Citi and $125 at JPM.

bullets.title: NVDA Positioning Turns Bearish; Removed as MS Top Pick After -25% Drop
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley removed NVDA as a Top Pick following a stop-loss trigger after the stock fell -25% from its October 2 peak; net crowding is at its lowest level since 2023 and 1-month put-call skew is at the 89th percentile. The implied earnings move stands at +/-7.7%, the highest since February 2025. Despite GB200/300 rack shipments +16% m/m in October, political headwinds (Senator Cramer calling for CEO Huang's resignation) weaken NVDA's lobbying position and the Chip Security Act is likely in the year-end NDAA.

bullets.title: AI Capex Now 41% of S&P 500 Cash Use; Bond Market Pricing Uncertainty
bullets.body: 22V Research notes AI capex accounts for 41% of S&P 500 total cash use, exceeding shareholder returns for the first time since 2021. AI credit spreads have widened from near-junk-tight in 2025 to wider than BB/B today, with $232B in hyperscaler and $42B in data-center HG bond issuance YTD (+160% y/y) and ~$103B in GPU financings in motion. AWS CEO confirmed supply constraints persist 2+ years and each 50% drop in inference costs drives an order-of-magnitude usage increase.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO at $917B–$1.4T Valuation Raises AI Liquidity Risk
bullets.body: Anthropic (ticker ANT) set an IPO range of $70–$78/share implying a $917B–$1.4T fully diluted valuation, with Q3 revenues of ~$17B (~12x YoY) and an $81B annualized run rate as of October 31. The offering includes a $26B concurrent private placement from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC; founder share class retains 50.1% voting control. Hedgeye questions whether the $500B annual revenue target — 6-7x current run rate — is achievable given diffusion, market-size, and compute constraints.

bullets.title: Post-Midterm AI Sell-Off Seen as Buyable; Texas Data Center Risk Overstated
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley and multiple strategists frame the post-midterm AI sell-off as a buying opportunity with capex outlook unchanged. Texas policy shifts could delay ~20% of 2028 US data center projects to 2029, but unpermitted Texas sites represent <2% of CRWV's 4.5GW contracted capacity. Hedge funds were undersold AI/semis after midterms with nets at 42% and sentiment overwhelmingly negative — a contrarian setup.

bullets.title: SpaceX Acquires 800 MHz Spectrum for ~$8B; Fourth Mobile Entrant Risk Rises
bullets.body: The FCC Wireless Telecommunications Bureau accepted Starlink's application to transfer 800 MHz SMRS licenses from Grain Management in an ~$8B cash deal, accelerating Starlink Mobile ambitions. Tower names (AMT, SBA, CCI) rallied as Wells Fargo noted SpaceX must build a hybrid satellite/terrestrial network using existing towers; Verizon is expected to spend ~$18B in the 2027 Upper C-Band auction, where SpaceX participation could inflate bidding. JPMorgan warns telecom sentiment will be hit by the prospect of a fourth entrant.

bullets.title: Sector Rotation: Comm Services and Industrials See Outflows; Healthcare Positive
bullets.body: JPM flow data shows Comm Services outflows of -$1.1B and Industrials -$1.1B on the session, while healthcare saw positive inflows. Retail net bought $1.6B (67.9th percentile) with preference for Mag7 over tech ex-Mag7; thematic ETFs saw heavy selling (-$2.1B, -1.3z) including DRAM, ALAI, and MAGS. HFs sold back ~70% of Monday's purchases with gross longs sold in excess of short adds.

bullets.title: AI Compute Oversupply Threat Growing; GPU Rental Rates Fallen 67% to ~$4/hr
bullets.body: Militia Capital's David Orr warns AI infrastructure faces further downside through 2028 as compute oversupply builds, citing GPU rental rates fallen from ~$12 to ~$4/hour anecdotally. He prefers hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft) on contracted capacity supporting ~35% ROI over pure-play AI infra. Software companies without strong moats risk losing pricing power as AI makes existing products cheaper to replicate.

bullets.title: CPU-to-GPU Ratio Set to Rise 1:8→1:1; Global CPU TAM Seen at $300B
bullets.body: Citi's Fujitsu MONAKA CTO roundtable highlights a structural shift in AI workloads: the CPU-to-GPU ratio is expected to rise from 1:8 to 1:1 or higher, driven by personal AI agent inference demand. MONAKA's core die is on TSMC 2nm with 5nm I/O via Broadcom 3D stacking, offering significant price advantages over Intel and AMD; global CPU TAM is projected to reach $300B. This is a potential headwind for GPU-centric revenue outlooks if inference shifts to CPUs.

bullets.title: PC Notebook Shipments -23% Y/Y in October; 2026 Outlook Cut Further
bullets.body: KeyBanc reports October PC notebook ODM shipments of 10.7M units (-22% m/m, -23% y/y), below the 11.5M estimate, with misses across Quanta, Compal, Wistron, and Inventec. Full-year 2026 outlook cut to -12-15% y/y from -10-15% on memory supply shortages and weak demand from price increases; 2027 expected to decline a further -8-12%. AMD, INTC, MU, and NVDA are negatively exposed.

bullets.title: Quant Factor Regimes Stressed; Momentum Undergoing 'Reset'
bullets.body: JPMorgan QIS flagged that factor regimes have experienced a volatile stretch with crowded positioning and momentum factors undergoing a 'reset.' Extreme rebalancing, leverage, and high turnover are driving implementation challenges, while de-grossing and crowding pain are creating unwind opportunities with regional performance disconnects.

bullets.title: Restaurant SSS Softest Since April; Consumer in Quad 4 Disinflation
bullets.body: Hedgeye data shows restaurant same-store sales decelerated to +1.5% YoY in October, 40bps below Q3 and the softest print since April, with traffic -1.8% YoY. Pricing power is fading as menu increases stand out against a Quad 4 disinflation backdrop, with no ticket payback for lost traffic — 26 of 36 restaurant names are bullish on quant signal but fundamentals are deteriorating.

bullets.title: Goldman Proposes Long Cyclicals / Lower European Yields Trade Post-Midterms
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs argues post-midterm developments have reduced extreme Middle East escalation risk that supported higher energy prices and yields. Brent crude has retraced sharply from recent highs alongside a decline in 2-year EUR swap rates, and European equities materially underperformed before rebounding sharply in early November. Goldman proposes leveraged dual-binary trades on SX5E and XLF targeting >105% by January 15, 2027 paired with EUR rates below current ATM.

bullets.title: US Lodging RevPAR +4.7% for Week Ending 11/7; 4Q26 Tracking +7.8%
bullets.body: US RevPAR rose +4.7% Y/Y for the week ending November 7 ($110 ADR, +3.2%; occupancy +1.4%), with Midscale chain-scale leading at +8.2%. 4Q26 is tracking +7.8% overall, well above consensus; HLT tracking +7.3% vs. consensus +4.5%, MAR +7.0% vs. +5.9%, and Hyatt +6.9% vs. +3.0%. Five of seven remaining 2026 weeks have easy comps from prior-year negatives.

bullets.title: Ace Hardware Q3 Comps Accelerate to +2.0%; Positive Read for HD, LOW
bullets.body: Mizuho flags Ace Hardware's Q3 comps of +2.0% (up from Q2's +1.1%) with two-year stacked trends improving >300bps, as a positive read-through for Home Depot and Lowe's earnings next week given >90% historical correlation since 2018. HD street estimates embed +1.5% domestic comps while LOW consensus is +0.4%; online comps at Ace were +12.0%.

bullets.title: SpaceX Starlink Contemplating T-Mobile Carrier Acquisition
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags that SpaceX's Starlink is contemplating a carrier acquisition with T-Mobile viewed as the logical choice, which would compress incumbent wireless margins and multiples. Combined with the 800 MHz spectrum deal, this signals an accelerating threat to terrestrial wireless pricing power across the sector.

bullets.title: SMR/Nuclear Names +6%+ on DOE Clearance; TLN Signs $365/MW-Day Capacity Deal
bullets.body: SMR and OKLO each rose ~6.4% after DOE clearance for Groves-1, while Talen Energy (TLN) surged +6.3% on a 750 MW long-term PJM capacity agreement (2029-2036) generating ~$100M annually at ~$365/MW-day — a constructive price above cap. Morgan Stanley notes VRT trailing twelve-month orders imply a $30B+ next-twelve-month revenue opportunity vs. consensus at $18.4B, suggesting ~60% upside.
